# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

I'll read the issue first.

{"number":1119,"title":"Migrate to the unified task:status:/task:origin: label scheme","body":"Tracking issue for the label-scheme migration. The end state and its rationale: `docs/label-scheme/DESIGN.md` (lands in #1120). This body is the plan — phases sorted by what blocks; append-only once implementation starts.

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup

- [x] None needed — confirmed: labels are created by the engine's ensure-if-missing pass with the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the stubs already declare `issues: write`. No secret, grant, or platform setting changes.

## Review pass — one stacked-PR arrival, base-first on #1120

- [ ] **PR 1 — read side + stubs** (additive, safe on every member in any order): the one-pass decode map (every legacy spelling → canonical status), new label constants and ensure-list entries, and the scheduler/executor stubs — canon's own `.github/workflows/` copies in the same commit — triggering on legacy *and* new ready/urgent spellings and filing failure issues as `task:origin:github` + `task:status:needs-human-failure`. Nothing writes a new label yet. Exit: merged, suite green against current `main`.
- [ ] **PR 2 — one-issue request mode**: adoption reads `task:origin:ad-hoc`-with-no-status beside `claude-task`, writes the machine block onto the marked issue, gates body parameters on the author's push access (collaborators-permission API), and the `Task:` targeting field lands with `add-packs` folded into it. Still writes legacy status spellings. Exit: merged.
- [ ] **PR 3 — write-side flip**: constants' values change to the new spellings (statuses; origins — generator writes `planned`, adoption `ad-hoc`, stubs `github`), janitor and dashboard follow, `claude-*` writes retire. Exit: merged — merge is gated on execution step 1 below.

Ran the fleet-wide label cleanup pass this issue's tail is waiting on, with GitHub issue read+write on all 14 active members. **Nothing was relabelled and no label was deleted** — three separate blockers, each read rather than assumed. Reporting all of it.

## How the fleet reads were made

The previous attempt on #1154 parked because "this session's GitHub access is scoped to `missingbulb/Claudinite` only". That is fixable from inside a session: `add_repo` (Claude Code Remote) widens this session's GitHub scope, and it did — all 14 members attached, and `list_issues`/`issue_read` against each returned normally. Fleet enumeration re-derived from `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` (`coverage.folding`, 14 repos incl. the canon; `coverage.dormant` = HelloWorldFlutterApp, gRatio, no mount). No read was refused, and no sweep came back empty or rate-limited.

## 1. #1154's remaining Verify leg — PASSES

No open `[claudinite-work]` item parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z names a label, a status, or a missing label as its cause. Read the park comments directly on Shepherd #205, ClaudiniteCanary #264, ClaudiniteWebsite #321, EdFringeNow #491, GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050, MissingBulbWebsite #240, TLDR #367, VascularColoring #258, hitbut #135 — spanning every member with a post-cutoff park and all four park kinds. The causes are four, none of them the label scheme:

- `converge-item.mjs` cannot authenticate — the dispatched session's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a proxy sentinel (401/403 "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"). This is the dominant cause, already tracked as #1133, #1149 and #1374.
- `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` not set (ClaudiniteCanary #264, `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`).
- `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` (GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050).
- No readable `.claudinite-settings.json`, status 404 (Shepherd #205).

Worth naming explicitly, because it reads like a counter-example and is not one: several of these items are **still wearing `task:agent`** (EdFringeNow #491, TLDR #367, MissingBulbWebsite #240, ClaudiniteWebsite #321). That label is the *residue* of a convergence that could not run — each session deliberately declined to hand-roll the swap — not the cause of the park. The janitor then escalated them on the 3h stale-agent rule. The decode reached them fine.

## 2. #1152 CANNOT be merged — its step-4 preconditions are false

Per #1154's playbook step 4, confirmed before merging rather than after. Two of the four conditions fail:

| Condition | Read |
|---|---|
| open | ✅ open, not draft |
| base is `main` | ✅ base `main` @ `f71ef81` |
| checks green | ⚠️ one check run, `test-and-conformance` success — but from **2026-08-21T11:33**, and `main` has taken **52 commits** since |
| GitHub reports it mergeable | ❌ **`mergeable_state: "dirty"`** |

Verified independently of the API: after `git fetch --unshallow`, `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/claude/claudinite-issue-1119-pr3-flip` returns **11 content conflicts** —

```
packs/basics/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-dashboard/{fleet,pack,ui,view-repo}.mjs
packs/claudinite-growth/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/queue/{executor-loop,scheduler-run,vocabulary}.test.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/tasks/task-janitor-queue-sweep.test.mjs
```

And the deeper problem: the PR's own body describes editing `engine/scheduler/queue/`. **That directory no longer exists on `main`** — the queue moved into `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` with the #1317 extraction. Git's rename detection still follows the flip onto the new paths, so the change is recoverable, but this is not a rebase-and-merge; it is a re-land onto a surface that moved underneath it, and the six-day-old green covers neither the new layout nor the 52 intervening commits.

**Not merged. #1154 left open**, and re-parked from `task:needs-human-action` to `task:needs-human-decision` — the enumeration blocker its old park named is gone, and what is left is a choice (re-land the flip on the moved layout, or supersede #1152) rather than a mechanical action.

## 3. The relabel and the deletions are both blocked — and the deletions would not have held anyway

**Relabel (closed issues, legacy → canonical): not performed.** The write-side flip has not merged, so no member's stamp can yet carry it; relabelling now just re-dirties as the still-legacy engine keeps writing legacy spellings. This is the ordering this issue's own plan sets, and it holds.

**Deleting the legacy label *definitions*: would be undone within a day, on every member.** `QUEUE_LABELS` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/work-item.mjs:323` still lists every legacy name — `task:blocked`, `task:ready`, `task:executing`, `task:agent`, `needs-human`, all four `task:needs-human-*`, `task:done`, `task:obsolete` — and `ensureLabels(gh, repo, QUEUE_LABELS)` runs from `scheduler-run.mjs:671,794`, `executor.mjs:618`, `create-work-item.mjs:97` and the janitor's `queue-sweep.mjs:53`. Every scheduler cycle in every member re-creates any of them that is missing. #1152 does not change this — its own body is explicit: *"They stay in the ensure-list too — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it."*

So deleting the definitions is not the tail of this migration; **dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` is**, and that is a separate change gated on 4(b) below reaching zero.

## 4. The two reads other issues are waiting on

### (a) For #1382 — open `[claudinite-task]` issues: **NOT zero. Three, across two members.**

- **EdFringeNow** — #363 `[claudinite-task] edfringe/refresh-tickets d2026-08-15`, #359 `[claudinite-task] grow_with_claudinite/growth-extract d2026-08-15`
- **VascularColoring** — #109 `[claudinite-task] core/update d2026-08-15~f31916551918` (also wears `escalation:apply-stage`)
- All other 12 members, canon included: **zero**.

Read from every open issue title in all 14 repos (not a search). #1382's removal is gated: deleting `ready-for-agent` / `ready-for-agent-fleet` / `agent-running` would strip them off these three, and deleting the janitor's two dispatch rules abandons them.

### (b) For this issue's tail — open work items still wearing a legacy status spelling: **NOT zero. ~176, on all 14 members.**

| Member | open items wearing a legacy status | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Claudinite | 33 | incl. #1086 also on `task:agent` |
| hitbut | 24 | all `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-action` |
| ClaudiniteCanary | 22 | incl. #133 `task:agent` |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | 15 | incl. #321 `task:agent` |
| VascularColoring | 14 | incl. #109, a `[claudinite-task]` |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | 12 | incl. #1076 `task:agent` |
| MissingBulbWebsite | 12 | |
| EdFringeNow | 11 | incl. #363, #359, `[claudinite-task]`s |
| CrosswordChat | 7 | |
| LaughCounter | 7 | |
| Shepherd | 6 | |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | 6 | |
| TLDR | 6 | |
| WIP | 1 | |

Every one of these is the `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-` pair, four are `task:agent`, and a long tail also carries `origin:schedule`. **The decode map's legacy entries cannot leave the engine.** They are not draining on their own either: the drain depends on convergence, and convergence is exactly what is broken fleet-wide (#1133 / #1149 / #1374). Until an item can converge, the legacy-wearing population grows rather than shrinks.

## What this leaves

The tail of this migration is blocked behind three things, in order:

1. **Convergence has to work** (#1149 / #1374). Nothing drains until it does, so 4(b) cannot reach zero.
2. **#1152 has to be re-landed** on the post-#1317 layout, re-verified against current `main` — a branch's own green never covers the whole-tree aggregate.
3. **Then** the closed-issue relabel, and only after that, dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` — which is what actually retires the definitions.

Not closing this issue, not editing its body.

**PR 3 has merged** — `a7e49ed0`, [#1385](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1385), not #1152. #1152 is closed: it was `dirty` with 11 conflicts and written against `engine/scheduler/queue/`, which #1317 moved. #1385 re-lands the same flip on the current layout, rebased onto `3541d6a` and verified there — 2722 tests pass, `check_the_work` clean, `check_the_world` 0 blocking / 87 advisory, identical to `origin/main` in a clean worktree.

One thing the re-land caught that the original branch could not have: `packs/claudinite-dashboard/work.mjs` and `next-work.mjs` postdate #1152 and used `NEEDS_HUMAN` as a **state key**, the same way `fleet.mjs` and `ui.mjs` did. Merged as-was, both would have compared `stateOf()`'s output against a label the engine no longer writes — no error, no failing test, and **zero parked items counted on both dashboards**. They move to `PARKED` with the rest, and `model.mjs` stops re-exporting the deprecated constant so the page side cannot reach for it again.

**Execution step 2 remains**, and is now filed as its own verification: [#1391](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1391), attached here as a sub-issue. It waits on ClaudiniteCanary's stamp reaching `packVersions.claudinite-tasks` ≥ `60827.3`, then reads that member's own issues to confirm a fresh scheduler cycle files items wearing exactly one `task:status:*`, one `task:origin:*`, and no legacy spelling. Retries daily until live. Forcing `fleet-baseline` with `follow` would bring that moment forward; the nightly converge gets there on its own otherwise.

**A correction to what I wrote earlier today.** My first comment framed "dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS`" as this migration's real tail. This issue's own body says otherwise, and it is right: *"Legacy label definitions are never deleted (deleting a label strips it from closed issues — stored data); the decode map is permanent."* So the label deletions I was asked to make are not merely blocked or futile against the nightly ensure pass — they were never part of the plan, and doing them would destroy stored data on closed issues fleet-wide. The genuine tail is the two items already in the body: removing legacy spellings from the stub triggers once no fielded engine writes them, and marking the legacy label series historical wherever counts are folded.

Ran the fleet-wide label cleanup pass this issue's tail is waiting on, with GitHub issue read+write on all 14 active members. **Nothing was relabelled and no label was deleted** — three separate blockers, each read rather than assumed. Reporting all of it.

## How the fleet reads were made

The previous attempt on #1154 parked because "this session's GitHub access is scoped to `missingbulb/Claudinite` only". That is fixable from inside a session: `add_repo` (Claude Code Remote) widens this session's GitHub scope, and it did — all 14 members attached, and `list_issues`/`issue_read` against each returned normally. Fleet enumeration re-derived from `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` (`coverage.folding`, 14 repos incl. the canon; `coverage.dormant` = HelloWorldFlutterApp, gRatio, no mount). No read was refused, and no sweep came back empty or rate-limited.

## 1. #1154's remaining Verify leg — PASSES

No open `[claudinite-work]` item parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z names a label, a status, or a missing label as its cause. Read the park comments directly on Shepherd #205, ClaudiniteCanary #264, ClaudiniteWebsite #321, EdFringeNow #491, GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050, MissingBulbWebsite #240, TLDR #367, VascularColoring #258, hitbut #135 — spanning every member with a post-cutoff park and all four park kinds. The causes are four, none of them the label scheme:

- `converge-item.mjs` cannot authenticate — the dispatched session's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a proxy sentinel (401/403 "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"). This is the dominant cause, already tracked as #1133, #1149 and #1374.
- `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` not set (ClaudiniteCanary #264, `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`).
- `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` (GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050).
- No readable `.claudinite-settings.json`, status 404 (Shepherd #205).

Worth naming explicitly, because it reads like a counter-example and is not one: several of these items are **still wearing `task:agent`** (EdFringeNow #491, TLDR #367, MissingBulbWebsite #240, ClaudiniteWebsite #321). That label is the *residue* of a convergence that could not run — each session deliberately declined to hand-roll the swap — not the cause of the park. The janitor then escalated them on the 3h stale-agent rule. The decode reached them fine.

## 2. #1152 CANNOT be merged — its step-4 preconditions are false

Per #1154's playbook step 4, confirmed before merging rather than after. Two of the four conditions fail:

| Condition | Read |
|---|---|
| open | ✅ open, not draft |
| base is `main` | ✅ base `main` @ `f71ef81` |
| checks green | ⚠️ one check run, `test-and-conformance` success — but from **2026-08-21T11:33**, and `main` has taken **52 commits** since |

```

```

And the deeper problem: the PR's own body describes editing `engine/scheduler/queue/`. **That directory no longer exists on `main`** — the queue moved into `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` with the #1317 extraction. Git's rename detection still follows the flip onto the new paths, so the change is recoverable, but this is not a rebase-and-merge; it is a re-land onto a surface that moved underneath it, and the six-day-old green covers neither the new layout nor the 52 intervening commits.

**Not merged. #1154 left open**, and re-parked from `task:needs-human-action` to `task:needs-human-decision` — the enumeration blocker its old park named is gone, and what is left is a choice (re-land the flip on the moved layout, or supersede #1152) rather than a mechanical action.

## 3. The relabel and the deletions are both blocked — and the deletions would not have held anyway

**Relabel (closed issues, legacy → canonical): not performed.** The write-side flip has not merged, so no member's stamp can yet carry it; relabelling now just re-dirties as the still-legacy engine keeps writing legacy spellings. This is the ordering this issue's own plan sets, and it holds.

So deleting the definitions is not the tail of this migration; **dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` is**, and that is a separate change gated on 4(b) below reaching zero.

### (a) For #1382 — open `[claudinite-task]` issues: **NOT zero. Three, across two members.**

Read from every open issue title in all 14 repos (not a search). #1382's removal is gated: deleting `ready-for-agent` / `ready-for-agent-fleet` / `agent-running` would strip them off these three, and deleting the janitor's two dispatch rules abandons them.

Every one of these is the `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-` pair, four are `task:agent`, and a long tail also carries `origin:schedule`. **The decode map's legacy entries cannot leave the engine.** They are not draining on their own either: the drain depends on convergence, and convergence is exactly what is broken fleet-wide (#1133 / #1149 / #1374). Until an item can converge, the legacy-wearing population grows rather than shrinks.

## What this leaves

The tail of this migration is blocked behind three things, in order:

1. **Convergence has to work** (#1149 / #1374). Nothing drains until it does, so 4(b) cannot reach zero.
2. **#1152 has to be re-landed** on the post-#1317 layout, re-verified against current `main` — a branch's own green never covers the whole-tree aggregate.
3. **Then** the closed-issue relabel, and only after that, dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` — which is what actually retires the definitions.

Not closing this issue, not editing its body.

{"number":1385,"title":"Label scheme PR 3, re-landed: write the canonical spellings","body":"Stage 3 of #1119 — the write-side flip. **Supersedes #1152**, which cannot merge: `mergeable_state: "dirty"`, 11 content conflicts, and its whole diff was written against `engine/scheduler/queue/`, a directory #1317 has since moved to `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/`. Its green also predated 52 commits on `main`.

The gate #1152 waited on is satisfied. #1154's `Verify:` now passes on all three legs — the two file legs were confirmed fleet-wide on 2026-08-24, and the third (no member parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z citing a label, a status or a missing label) was read this session across all 14 active members. The parks are `converge-item.mjs` auth failures, a missing `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, a `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` and one 404 — none of them the label scheme. Full reads: #1119.

## What flips

- **The write constants hold today's spellings** — statuses, terminals, and the origin on every born item. Their *names* survive because fielded pack versions import them: a pack still on the old engine writes a legacy label, which every decoder reads as what it always meant.
- **A park stops being a pair.** `needs-human` + a sub-label could be half-applied — a torn state of its own — so a park is one `task:status:needs-human-`, written by one swap. Executor, session converge, scheduler reclaim and the janitor's sweep all follow.
- **The legacy spellings become explicit `LEGACY_*` literals.** The decode map was built from the constants that just moved; left alone it would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten the vocabulary it exists to read. They stay in `QUEUE_LABELS` — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue carrying it.
- **The dashboard gets its own `PARKED` display key** rather than borrowing a label nothing writes.
- **The re-queue lever is one exported phrase** — clearing the status *is* the re-ask.
- **Writer-facing prose swept**: the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, and `writing-tasks`.

## What this re-land adds over #1152

`packs/claudinite-dashboard/work.mjs` and `next-work.mjs` did not exist when the flip was first written. Both used `NEEDS_HUMAN` as a **state key** exactly as `fleet.mjs` and `ui.mjs` did, so a straight rebase would have left them comparing `stateOf()`'s output against a label the engine no longer writes — no error, no failing test, just **zero parked items counted on both dashboards**. They are converted to `PARKED` with the rest. `model.mjs` also stops re-exporting the now-deprecated `NEEDS_HUMAN`, so the same mistake cannot be made again from the page side.

The scheduler's reclaim also drops its separate `op.triage` write — with a one-label park, nothing produces `op.triage` any more, and the line was a dead read.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/     the write constants and the LEGACY_* literals, the
                            one-label park, origins on every born item, the shared
                            re-queue phrase, and the session/worker briefs that tell
                            an agent what to write. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ the parked state becomes the page's own PARKED key across
                            all five modules that read it. Version bumped.
packs/basics/               the janitor's sweep writes one park label. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-growth/    writing-tasks states today's vocabulary. Version bumped.
```

## Verification

Re-run after rebasing onto `3541d6a` — against **current `main`**, not the branch's own base:

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2722 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_work` — **0 blocking, 0 advisory**.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 87 advisory**, identical to the same command run on `origin/main` in a clean worktree. No finding is introduced by this change.

Every failure the flip caused was write-assertion churn (`task:done` → `task:status:done`, `task:ready` → `task:status:waiting-for-executor`, `task:blocked` → `task:status:blocked`, and a born item now wearing its origin), fixed in place. `vocabulary.test.mjs` carries the write side: every write constant is a canonical status, a park is one label, a kind word resolves to it, and the re-queue phrase names clearing the status.

The rebase also picked up #1373/#1377, which removed the dependent release from convergence — so the flip's re-spelling of a label a converge no longer writes was dropped rather than carried.

## What this does NOT do

It does not relabel anything, and it deletes no label definition. Both are #1119's tail and both are still blocked — the relabel on this landing plus a fleet converge, and the deletions on `QUEUE_LABELS` dropping the legacy names, which cannot happen while ~176 open items fleet-wide still wear them. See #1119 for the per-member picture.

input.body:
Tracking issue for the label-scheme migration. The end state and its rationale: `docs/label-scheme/DESIGN.md` (lands in #1120). This body is the plan — phases sorted by what blocks; append-only once implementation starts.

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup

- [x] None needed — confirmed: labels are created by the engine's ensure-if-missing pass with the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the stubs already declare `issues: write`. No secret, grant, or platform setting changes.

## Review pass — one stacked-PR arrival, base-first on #1120

- [x] **PR 1 — read side + stubs** (additive, safe on every member in any order): the one-pass decode map (every legacy spelling → canonical status), new label constants and ensure-list entries, and the scheduler/executor stubs — canon's own `.github/workflows/` copies in the same commit — triggering on legacy *and* new ready/urgent spellings and filing failure issues as `task:origin:github` + `task:status:needs-human-failure`. Nothing writes a new label yet. Exit: merged, suite green against current `main`.
- [x] **PR 2 — one-issue request mode**: adoption reads `task:origin:ad-hoc`-with-no-status beside `claude-task`, writes the machine block onto the marked issue, gates body parameters on the author's push access (collaborators-permission API), and the `Task:` targeting field lands with `add-packs` folded into it. # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Author: missingbulb <73882448+missingbulb@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sun Aug 23 14:30:14 2026 +0300

    Gate wiki-growth on pending product-wiki paths, not a label (#1257)
    
    The `product-wiki-growth` label existed for one reader: the wiki-growth
    precondition, declining while a previous round's PR sat unreviewed. Every
    growth PR carried a marker nothing else looked at, and a PR opened without
    it was silently stacked on.
    
    The `prs` collector now resolves each open PR's changed paths, and the
    precondition declines on a pending `product-wiki/` change in any open PR —
    a human's edit in flight as much as the task's own. Paths that could not be
    read are `null`, a third state the gate declines on rather than reading as
    clear, which is also what carries it through an engine older than this one.
    
    `prs.open[].labels` goes with the label: it was there for this gate alone.
    
    Closes #1256

input.title: Label scheme PR 4 — the vocabulary sweep over live prose and check catalogs
input.body:
The last unbuilt box of #1119's review pass. Its two halves have diverged since the plan was written:

**Half 1 — product-wiki's gate — already delivered, by another route.** The plan said the gate should read its own approval-parked item instead of a labeled PR. `c0dd572` ([#1257](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1257), closing #1256) got there first and better: the `prs` collector now resolves each open PR's changed paths and the precondition declines on a pending `product-wiki/` change in *any* open PR — a human's wiki edit in flight gates the round too, which an item-marker read never would. `product-wiki-growth` is gone, and `prs.open[].labels` went with it. Nothing left to do.

**Half 2 — the vocabulary sweep — outstanding.** [#1385](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1385) swept the three briefs it touched (the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, `writing-tasks`). What it did not reach is every *other* writer-facing document that still tells an agent to write the retired **pair** — `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-<kind>` — or names a legacy status as the current one. A park has been one label since `a7e49ed0`; a brief that still asks for two is asking for a torn state the janitor then has to repair.

## Scope

Sweep, because each is read by an agent at run time and states today's vocabulary:

- `packs/claudinite-growth/skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md` — the terminal-outcome section still says `task:obsolete`.
- `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.md`, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/README.md`
- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/tasks/fleet-digest/task.md`, `packs/basics/tasks/ci-performance/task.md`, `packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/growth-dedup/task.md`
- `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/README.md` and its four task READMEs
- `packs/claudinite-growth/declared-checks.json` — the check catalog's `fix` text
- `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` — only the lines stating today's mechanism in the pair form

Do **not** sweep, and say why in the PR:

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/executor.md` — the retired slot mechanism's brief, deliberately frozen for routines nobody has repointed. Its vocabulary is that scheme's, not this one's.
- `docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md`, `docs/per-project-scheduling/*`, `docs/task-code-work/DESIGN.md`, `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` — records of play-throughs and superseded schemes.
- `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` §4's legacy decode table and §15's decision records — the decode map is permanent, and a decision record says what was decided when.
- every `VERSIONS.md`, and `on_interrupt: 'needs-human'`, which is a declaration value and not a label.

## The assurance

`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/queue/vocabulary.test.mjs` gains a scan over the live briefs for the pair form and for legacy status spellings, with the exclusions above named explicitly in the test — so the next brief written against the old vocabulary fails rather than reaching a member.

Closes the **PR 4 — ride-alongs** box of #1119.

content.content:
**An open item is the task's standing item, and a `failure` park therefore stops
  the task being scheduled** — no further occurrence is filed until it is woken or
  closed. That is deliberate: a queue of items that will break the same way helps
  nobody, and the silence is the signal. The other three do **not** hold the lane —
  they are one person's inbox, not a fault in the task, so the schedule carries on
  around them.
- **Never ran** → `task:obsolete`, closed as not planned: the precondition
  declined, or the task is gone (file removed, pack undeclared). An obsolete item
  is not an anomaly and gets no `needs-human`. A scheduled task's next occurrence
  is the scheduler run's ask at its next anchor — and most declines never make an
  item at all: the scheduler run asks the precondition when the anchor comes,
  files an item only on a yes, and records a no as a row on the repo's schedule
  board (the one open `[claudinite-schedule]` issue).
- Every terminal state is recorded in code as a `claudinite-task-exec` line
  (`record-exec.mjs`), so the usage fold counts task statuses out of the captured
  conversation logs deterministically.
=== 230-250 ===
  an open PR elsewhere. If a condition should stop the run, it belongs in the
  precondition, as code over signals, its verdict binding via the item's
  Context.
- **Failures may stop a run** — a crash, a timeout, an API error park the
  item at `needs-human`. Discretion may not.
- **A failing worker may say why it failed.** The executor sees an exit code and
  nothing more, so it cannot tell a token missing a scope (a person's five-second
  fix) from an exception in the worker's own code (a bug). A worker that knows
  prints one line on either stream before exiting non-zero, and the park is routed
  by it:

  ```
  claudinite-needs-human: action — FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN lacks Actions: write
  ```

day. What stays with the janitor is everything needing judgment or a longer

`task:status:needs-human-decision`),
and the health review, which gains the queue (ready-item age, blocked-item
depth, outcome mix) as its subject and can now compute all of it from
6. **Endpoint tokens ride the same rail** (§12): config maps endpoint name →
   URL + the *name* of the Actions secret; the executor reads that name out of the
   bag at the moment of the API call and nowhere else. The CCR session-creation
   token is simply the default endpoint's entry.
7. **Missing secret** — absent from the bag: baselining asks the
   owner on its standing issue (the adoption-interview posture), and until
   set, execution parks the affected item `needs-human` +
   `task:status:needs-human-action` naming the missing secret — at the work step for `required_secrets`, at hand-off for an
   endpoint token. Nothing fails silently; the task just doesn't work yet.
8. **Rotation** — rotate the value in repo settings; nothing else changes,
   because names are the interface everywhere above.
**A read failure is not a verdict.** A refusal's write-back (§16.5) cannot
reach an issue it cannot read, so declining on a transient API failure (a rate
limit, a 500) would strand the adopted status on the issue forever over nothing —
the request silently eaten. Only a definitive *gone* declines; any other read
failure **fails the run**: the item parks `needs-human` +
`task:status:needs-human-failure`, open and visible, and the ordinary re-queue lever
(§4) retries it once the API recovers.

content.content:
for a fresh repo, baselining's wiring converge for an established one — and
its wiring is exactly four things, all idempotent, all from the vendored
engine at HEAD:

1. **Labels**, create-if-missing: `task:status:waiting-for-executor/blocked/executing/agent/urgent`,
   `needs-human` and its four sub-labels (until #1050 retires the bare label),
   and the terminal pair `task:status:done`/`task:status:rejected`. Nothing ensures
   `outcome:delivered` — nothing applies it; decoders still read it and every
   other legacy spelling.
2. **Two vendored workflows**: the scheduler run (cron at the repo's stable hashed
   minute, plus `workflow_dispatch` so an operator or a migration never waits
   ones. #515's rationale does not survive the pull model.
3. **Timing in a precondition is advisory, not forbidden** (§6.4): permitted
   where the verdict cannot flip between creation and pickup for scheduling
   reasons alone. No check — the property is not mechanically checkable, and
   the residual failure is a visible `task:obsolete`, not a wrong result.
4. **A precondition is go/no-go, never maybe-later** (§5) — *changed the
   design twice*. First cut: one verdict per occurrence at the first scheduler run
read, never inside `anchorInstant`. A frequency is read by more than the calendar: `periodMs`
feeds the janitor's stale-ready bound (`queue/janitor-rules.mjs`, `staleReadyPeriods` × period)
and the precondition's signal window (`queue/signals.mjs`, period + an hour of slack). Normalizing
only the anchor would leave `periodMs('hourly')` returning an hour, so a task that now runs daily
would be judged stale after two HOURS and see a two-hour signal window — a spurious `needs-human`
park on every member still declaring the old token, which is precisely the population the
tolerance exists for.

input.title: Label scheme PR 4: sweep the writer-facing vocabulary
input.head: claude/issue-1119-status-check-96ybsv
input.body:
The last unbuilt box of #1119's review pass.

## Half 1 — product-wiki's gate — nothing to do

The plan said the gate should read its own approval-parked item instead of a labeled PR. `c0dd572` (#1257, closing #1256) got there first, and by a better route: the `prs` collector resolves each open PR's changed paths, and the precondition declines on a pending `product-wiki/` change in **any** open PR — so a human's wiki edit in flight gates the round too, which an item-marker read never would. `product-wiki-growth` is gone and `prs.open[].labels` went with it. Verified against the file, not the commit message.

## Half 2 — the sweep

#1385 swept the three briefs it touched. What it did not reach is every other document an agent reads **at run time** that still asks for the retired pair — `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-<kind>`. A park has been one label since `a7e49ed0`, so a brief still asking for two is asking for the torn state §6.2's repair rule exists to clean up.

Swept: `writing-tasks` (which also still named `task:obsolete` as the never-ran terminal, now `task:status:rejected`), the `update` brief and the updates README, the `fleet-digest`, `ci-performance` and `growth-dedup` briefs, sheepdog's README and its four task READMEs, `task-phase-discipline`'s remedy line, and the lines in `tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` that state today's mechanism in the pair form.

Deliberately **not** swept, each because the legacy spelling is the point there:

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/executor.md` — the retired slot mechanism's instructions, kept for routines nobody has repointed. Its `agent-running` / `needs-human` vocabulary is that scheme's, and rewriting it would break the sessions it is kept for.
- `docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md`, `docs/per-project-scheduling/*`, `docs/task-code-work/DESIGN.md`, `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` — records of play-throughs and superseded schemes.
- DESIGN §4's legacy decode table and §15's decision records — the decode map is permanent, and a decision record says what was decided when.
- every `VERSIONS.md`; and `on_interrupt: 'requeue' | 'needs-human'`, a declaration value rather than a label (its one prose mention is now quoted as the value it is).

## The assurance, written first

`vocabulary.test.mjs` gains two scans — over pack prose and over the check catalogs' agent-facing fields — built from the `LEGACY_*` constants rather than a hand-copied list, and reading the tracked tree so a brief added later is covered without being listed. Both failed on `main` (12 offending briefs, one remedy) before any file was touched.

## One thing this leaves open, deliberately

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/terminals.mjs` returns `label: NEEDS_HUMAN` and `tasks/update/worker.mjs` applies it — to the update **PR**, not to a work item. That is a live write of the bare legacy label, but it is code and a cross-repo convention rather than prose, so it is out of this PR's scope. Filed as #1396.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/    the two vocabulary scans (test only — nothing vendored changes)
packs/claudinite-growth/   writing-tasks' terminal and park spellings; the
                           task-phase-discipline remedy. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/ the update brief's park section and the updates README.
                           Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/ the pack README and four task READMEs say a failed
                           sweep parks. Version bumped.
packs/basics/              the ci-performance brief's missing-input park. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ the fleet-digest brief's missing-input park. Version bumped.
docs/                      tasks-dispatch DESIGN's live statements only.
```

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2728 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_work` — clean.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 87 advisory**, the same count `main` carries.

Closes #1395
Refs #1119

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
